Our best algorithm, Triple-Color , though outperforming PI-SAGE , is still outperformed by classical methods, such as that of [ 13 ] . Additionally, though the performance of Full-GCN scales well as the order of the graph increases to about 1000 1000 , it is quite slow even to run Mod-GCN for graphs this large, much less Full-GCN . A natural future direction is to continue finding new modifications to the GNN method that further improve its performance. Another is to test other GNN architectures beyond message-passing, such as graph transformers. Finally, it may be interesting to continue studying how the performance of each method scales as the order of the graph increases, and to find a new method for which the expected loss grows linearly with a small slope for n n as large as possible.
